nodes.summary: For a group $G$ acting on a set $\Omega$, a finite set $B \subseteq \Omega$ is a base when its pointwise stabilizer is trivial: the only $g \in G$ with $g \cdot \omega = \omega$ for all $\omega \in B$ is $g = 1$.
nodes.title: Base of a group action

nodes.summary: A finite subset $S$ of a group $G$ is independent when no element $s \in S$ lies in the subgroup of $G$ generated by $S \setminus \{s\}$.
nodes.title: Independent subset of a group

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ acting on a set $\Omega$, a finite set $B \subseteq \Omega$ is a minimal base when it is a base, that is, its pointwise stabilizer in $G$ is trivial, and for every $\omega \in B$ the set $B \setminus \{\omega\}$ is not a base.
nodes.title: Minimal base

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, a finite subset $S \subseteq G$ is independent when no $s \in S$ lies in the subgroup generated by $S \setminus \{s\}$. The number $\mu'(G)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the finite independent subsets of $G$: their largest size when these sizes are bounded, as they are for finite $G$, and $0$ when they are unbounded.
nodes.title: Maximal size of an independent set

nodes.summary: It is not true that $b(G) = \mu'(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $b(G)$ is the largest size of a minimal base of $G$ over all actions of $G$ on a set, and $\mu'(G)$ is the largest size of an independent subset of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.45 has a negative answer

nodes.summary: The statement that $b(G) = \mu'(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $b(G)$ is the largest size of a minimal base of $G$ over all actions of $G$ on a set, and $\mu'(G)$ is the largest size of an independent subset of $G$ (a subset none of whose elements lies in the subgroup generated by the others).
nodes.title: Cameron's question on minimal bases and independent sets

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the number $b(G)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the minimal bases of $G$ over all actions of $G$ on a set $\Omega$, where a minimal base is a finite set $B \subseteq \Omega$ whose pointwise stabilizer in $G$ is trivial while that of $B \setminus \{\omega\}$ is not, for every $\omega \in B$. can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
